target_customer: Teens and young adults learning to code (originally as MakeGamesWithUs), later students paying through income share agreements
problem: Students wanted practical software skills; Make School started with iOS game tutorials and summer programs and grew into a product-focused college alternative.
business_model: Tuition and income share agreements for its programs, earlier paid summer programs and tutorials
product_category: Education, coding school and college alternative

founders.name: Ashutosh Desai
education: UCLA, left after one year of computer science
founders.background_notes: SD Times 2015-06 says he built an iOS game in high school and studied CS for a year at UCLA; Wikipedia says he went to Menlo School.

founders.name: Jeremy Rossmann
founders.background_notes: Education per Wikipedia. YC page says he is later at Taiyaki Studios.

exit.reason: Co-founder Rossmann told Yahoo Finance in July 2021 that the for-profit Make School PBC was shutting down, handed the bachelor program to a nonprofit and cancelled its ISA program. No reason is given in sources opened.

competitors.name: Codecademy
competitors.what: Free interactive online coding lessons with gamified progress
competitors.traction_then: Over 1 million sign-ups and 400,000 users on the Code Year program

competitors.name: Treehouse
competitors.what: Paid online lessons in web design, development and iOS apps
competitors.traction_then: About 8,000 paid users at 25 or 49 dollars a month

technical_complexity.rationale: Content, curriculum and operations rather than hard technology.

defensibility.rationale: Curriculum and brand were copyable; the degree-granting path later depended on partner accreditation.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Not absorbed by incumbents. The company later faced regulatory trouble over operating as an unapproved school.

market_need_then: Rising interest in learning to code and iOS development in 2012, shown by coverage of Codecademy's million sign-ups.

branding.name_origin: Started as MakeGamesWithUs and renamed Make School in 2014 when the mission broadened, per Wikipedia; the origin of the first name is not given.

rebrands.why: Mission broadened to a gap year program, per Wikipedia

brand_strength.rationale: Little brand-specific press was found; coverage focused on the model and founders.

pivots.from: iOS game tutorials and summer camps (MakeGamesWithUs)
pivots.to: Make School gap year then two-year Product College
pivots.why: Mission change toward replacing college, per Wikipedia

pivots.from: For-profit Make School PBC with ISAs
pivots.to: Operations handed to a nonprofit, ISA program cancelled
pivots.why: Wind-down, reason not stated in sources opened

outcome_analysis: Make School began as MakeGamesWithUs in YC W12 and pivoted in 2014 into a degree alternative, raising a 15M Series B led by Venrock in 2019 for a 30M total. In 2021 the for-profit entity wound down, handed the program to a nonprofit and cancelled income share agreements. Sources point to regulatory trouble over operating without approval in California, but the company's stated reason was not found, so the unit economics label is tentative.
notes: makeschool.com safety check was rate-limited so the site was not opened. Wikipedia and the Make School release disagree on founding year (2012 vs 2014). Wikipedia says the program moved to Dominican University of California in Aug 2021; Yahoo via search says to a nonprofit. A dead-startups site claims an ABC insolvency proceeding; unverified and not used. Total raised: release says 30M, CB Insights 29.27M over 8 rounds, Wellfound 4.4M; earlier seed rounds from 500 Startups, Andreessen Horowitz, Learn Capital, Kapor Capital are named in SD Times 2015 without amounts, so rounds are missing. The Tech Review article from 2012-03 does not mention MakeGamesWithUs; Codecademy and Treehouse are adjacent players in the same coding education space.
